Thank you for your time earlier today on our Teams call. Here’s a summary of our screening demo discussion regarding your request to export single-listed ASX companies and dual-listed ASX companies (such as Rio Tinto) into a single screen or multiple screens, and easy ways to combine them. Since Lara wasn't available to call earlier, I will be taking over the case. Workaround Steps We Tried and was provided by Lara: We followed these steps in CIQ Pro: Click Browse Criteria from the left-hand panel, or use the search bar for Add Criteria and then click Browse Criteria at the bottom. In the Field Selector tool, navigate to Securities Summary > Equities > Security Information > Traded Issue . Under Parameters, select Yes for Traded Issue? Under Parameters, select Secondary Listings for Criteria Applies To. Click Add . Add Exchange > ASX . Click Done . Note: Using this method, companies like Rio Tinto Group and KMD Brands Limited did not appear in the results on CIQ Pro. To confirm, I shared my screen and navigated the same criteria in CIQ Legacy, where the companies you’re looking for were successfully pulled. Alternative Solution: I discovered another workaround by using the Securities Screen ( Application ) instead of the Companies Screen in CIQ Pro. With this method, companies/issuers such as Rio Tinto and KMD Brands were reflected in the results when using only the criteria Exchange > ASX . You may export this data as well. Next Steps: For further review regarding why secondary listings of certain companies aren’t reflecting in the Companies Screen, I will escalate this to our data team for investigation. Please let me know if you need further assistance or have additional questions. I’ll keep you updated once I hear back from the data team

Screening Steps I have created a Transaction screen for you titled "Buy-Side M&A Fees." To navigate this, please follow the steps below
In the top-right corner of the CIQ Pro platform, click the Screener
At the bottom of Key Workflows, select Manage Screens > Click on the mentioned saved screen
Click on Run Screen to view results. I have also showed the client how to navigate the Transaction screener. Here are the steps in replicating the screen for your reference
In the top navigation bar, click on Screener > Select Transactions
In the left handlings, click on Browse Criteria
Search for the keyfield: IQ_INDUSTRY_CLASSIFICATION > In: Energy and Industrials > Applies to: Target/Issuer > Add
Search for the keyfield: SPTR_TRANSACTION_VALUE > Between: 0
Search for the keyfield: SPTR_CLOSED_DATE > Set the timeframe

Search for the keyfield: SPTR_ADVISER_FEE > Greater than: 0 > Adviser Role: Financial Advisory > Party Advised: Buyer/Investor > Add > Done. Thank you for understanding! Currency and Magnitude You can change the currency at the top part of the screener. Alternatively, currency and magnitude can be changed by clicking on the Settings. Criteria vs Display Columns Criteria will filter the results, so only records that meet these criteria will be included and anything that does not meet them will be filtered out. Display columns control which columns are shown, regardless of whether they contain data, and they do not affect the number of results returned. Transaction Value vs Total Transaction Value vs Deal Value You may find the definition of the criteria in the screener. For the mentioned keyfields, here are the differences: Transaction Value [KeyField: 300198, SPTR_DEAL_TRANSACTION_VALUE] Deal value paid for equity, plus the value of assumed current liabilities, net of current assets Total Transaction Value [KeyField: 300057, SPTR_TRANSACTION_VALUE] For M&A, this is the consideration accrued to the seller for all target securities, including assumed liabilities. For capital offerings, this is the principal amount of capital raised in the offering, before fees and other expenses, including any amounts not sold directly by the issuer and exercised overallotment options. For rounds of funding and private M&A deals, this will also include estimated values (e.g. values disclosed by sources close to the matter reported in news or press or rumored values). For equity buybacks, this is the price paid for equity repurchased by company. For spin-offs or split-offs, this is the distribution value of target equity distributed to the seller’s shareholders.​​​​​​​ Deal Value [KeyField: 300194, SPTR_DEAL_VALUE] Total consideration accrued to the sellers. Includes only the price paid for equity, not assumption of any obligations of the entity sold. For Spin-off/ Split-offs, this field indicates distribution value of the transaction

https://spglobal.my.site.com/s/article/Dashboards The S&P Capital IQ Pro Dashboard application is meant to serve as an informational tool that can quickly provide data that is constantly changing in the global markets. The Dashboard is a fully customizable application, and provides you with the tools to create a solution that is meaningful to your workflow and helps with market monitoring. Creating Watch Lists

https://spglobal.my.site.com/s/article/Creating-List-of-Companies-or-Assets-using-My-Lists-on-MI Static lists are usable in Screener criteria, on the dashboard, in alert creation, in the chart builder, and across many other tools on the platform. When added to the Chart Builder, static lists are only able to uploaded as a custom index and cannot be charted as independent entities. Dynamic lists are purely generated by saving Screener results but cannot be used on any tools in the platform due to the nature of their potentially varying outcome of entities due to data being updated.
